adds.title: Istanbul Pride - Wikipedia
adds.summary: Wikipedia's 'Istanbul Pride' article documents that since 2015 İstanbul pride parades have been denied permission and locally banned by the Governorship of İstanbul on security-and-public-order grounds (2016-2018 bans explicitly, water cannon used on 29 June 2015), and that 2014 was the biggest LGBT event in Turkey's history with over 100,000 participants. It records the escalating police suppression with numbers: blockades and tear gas in 2021 with 25 arrested; 373 arrested in 2022 with public transport to Taksim Square shut down; 113 arrests in 2023; and 11 arrests in 2024 (three of them minors) after organisers moved Istanbul Pride to non-Taksim public spaces and issued fake meeting calls to thwart police. This frames the record's 'banned for a ninth consecutive year' claim with a per-year detention tally a visitor can weigh.

adds.title: Turkish police detain 373 LGBTI pride protestors in Istanbul
adds.summary: Duvar English (27 June 2022) reports that on 26 June 2022 riot police dispersed the Pride march in İstanbul's Taksim Square, blockaded streets in the nearby Cihangir neighbourhood, shut down public transport to the square, and detained 373 people - including AFP photojournalist Bülent Kılıç - who were released after a night in custody, according to Kaos GL. The district governor's offices of Kadıköy and Beyoğlu in İstanbul had banned all LGBTI+ Pride Week events for seven days, and eight more people were detained at a Pride march in İzmir. The piece states Pride has been banned by Turkish authorities since 2014 and that police crackdowns on the parades have grown harsher over the years.
